subject.title: fix(ollama): preserve custom memory provider endpoints

question: Should existing Ollama memory indexes automatically rebuild once on upgrade so base URL and identity-bearing headers become part of their canonical provider key?
rationale: The patch fixes silent stale-cache reuse and proves normal recovery, but it deliberately changes persisted identity for every existing Ollama index; accepting that upgrade cost is an owner decision rather than a correctness question.

options.title: Accept Canonical Rebuild
options.body: Merge the current design and accept one automatic rebuild so all Ollama indexes use endpoint-scoped identity consistently.

options.title: Preserve Default Keys
options.body: Revise the identity encoding to retain the old hash for implicit default-endpoint configurations while still distinguishing custom endpoints and headers.

options.title: Pause The Change
options.body: Leave the current cache identity unchanged if the upgrade-time rebuild cost outweighs the stale-cache correctness benefit.

recommendation.title: Accept Canonical Rebuild
recommendation.body: Merge the current design and accept one automatic rebuild so all Ollama indexes use endpoint-scoped identity consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history introduced and maintained the built-in Ollama memory adapter and its cache-identity behavior.
